key_insight: Ideal liquid crystal elastomers couple mesogen orientation and network deformation, enabling reversible actuation and finite deformation at nearly zero stress.
engineering_relevance: The theory provides a constitutive foundation for modeling soft actuators and predicting stretch-dependent mechanical responses in liquid crystal elastomers.
method: Bridge anisotropic Gaussian chain statistics with neo-classical continuum elasticity.
Explain spontaneous deformation and soft elasticity through stress-free states and coexisting stripe domains.
Use quasi-convex energy relaxation to classify polydomain behavior into three mechanical phases.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a theoretical review and three-phase classification, but reports no experimental datasets or quantitative validation metrics.
watch_item: Ideal behavior assumes no memory of the crosslinking state; realistic predictions may require nonideality, director-gradient, and viscoelastic contributions.
paper_title: Elastic theory of ideal liquid crystal elastomers
